subject: Money
title: The U.S. Housing Bubble
description: A short lesson to help you apply The U.S. Housing Bubble.

hook.text: Las Vegas home prices rose 134% between 2000 and 2006. Then they fell 62%. Entire neighborhoods were abandoned.

buildup.text: Easy credit, liar loans, and speculation turned houses into lottery tickets. Flippers bought and resold homes fast.

discovery.text: Banks stopped checking if borrowers could pay. No income? No problem. The loan was approved anyway.

twist.text: When prices fell, underwater homeowners walked away. Banks held homes they couldn't sell. The financial system froze.

climax.text: The housing crash caused the worst recession since the 1930s. Eight million jobs lost. A generation scarred.

punchline.text: Houses are shelter. They became casino chips.
